{{Short description|69th season of the National Hurling League}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox GAA League |league = 2000 National Hurling League |image = |dates = 20 February – 28 May 2000 |teams = 33 |team1 = Galway |captain1 = [[Joe Rabbitte]] |manager1 = [[Mattie Murphy]] |titles = 7th |team2 = Tipperary |captain2 = [[Tommy Dunne]] |manager2 = [[Nicky English]] |two= Meath |three = Louth |previous = [[1999 National Hurling League|1999]] |next = [[2001 National Hurling League|2001]] }} The '''2000 National Hurling League''', known for sponsorship reasons as the '''[[Allianz|Church & General]] National Hurling League''', was the 69th edition of the [[National Hurling League]] (NHL), an annual [[hurling]] competition for the [[GAA county teams]].[http://homepage.eircom.net/~gaelicgames/ Gaelic Games] [[Galway GAA|Galway]] won the league, beating [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the final.{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|title=National Hurling League Results 1925-2009|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=18 April 2011|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100805063526/http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|archivedate=5 August 2010}} ==Overview== ===Division 1=== The National Hurling League's top division featured fourteen teams divided into two groups - 1A and 1B. Each group consisted of seven teams. [[Galway GAA|Galway]] and [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] topped division 1A while [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] and [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] topped division 1B. Galway finished the league undefeated and were crowned champions after defeating Tipp in the final. Down at the other end of the tables, [[Kerry GAA|Kerry]] and [[Derry GAA|Derry]] failed to win a single group game and were paired against each other in the relegation play-off. Derry won that game, thus condemning Kerry to division 2 for the following year. ===Division 2=== Division 2 featured one group of ten teams. [[Carlow GAA|Carlow]] and [[Meath GAA|Meath]] topped the group and contested the final. Meath won and secured promotion to division 1A for the following year. [[Tyrone GAA|Tyrone]] ended the group stage without a single victory and were relegated to division 3 for the following year. ===Division 3=== Division 3 featured one group of nine teams. [[Louth GAA|Louth]] finished the group stages undefeated and were joined in the final by [[Longford GAA|Longford]] who recorded just one defeat. Louth won that game and secured promotion to division 2 for the following year. ==Division 1== {{Infobox football league season |competition=[[National Hurling League|National Hurling League Division 1]] |season=2000 |winners=[[Galway GAA|Galway]]

[[Derry GAA|Derry]] entered Division 1 as the promoted team. On 14 May 2000, [[Galway GAA|Galway]] won the title following a 2-18 to 2-13 win over Tipperary in the final. It was their first league title since [[1995-96 National Hurling League|1995-96]] and their sixth National League title overall. [[Kerry GAA|Kerry]], who lost all of their group stage matches, were relegated from Division 1 after losing the relegation play-off to Derry by 1-21 to 2-4. [[Meath GAA|Meath]] won Division 2 and secured promotion to the top tier. Galway's [[Fergal Healy]] was the Division 1 top scorer with 8-27. ===Structure=== The 14 teams in Division 1 were divided into two groups of seven teams named Division 1A and Division 1B. Each team played all the others in its group once. Two points were awarded for a win and one for a draw. The first two teams in 1A and 1B advanced to the league semi-finals with the top team in Division 1A playing the second team in Division 1B and the second team in Division 1A playing the first in Division 1B.
